questions.prompt: A wave travels along a stretched string. Is it transverse or longitudinal?
questions.answer: A string wave is transverse because the string elements move across the direction the disturbance travels.

questions.prompt: Sound travels through air as a sequence of compressions and rarefactions. Is this transverse or longitudinal?
questions.answer: It is longitudinal because the air parcels oscillate back and forth along the same line as the sound wave propagates.

questions.prompt: A periodic wave has frequency \(15\,\mathrm{Hz}\) and wavelength \(0.40\,\mathrm{m}\). Find the wave speed.
A disturbance moves to the right while each element of the medium moves up and down. Classify the wave and explain the geometric reason in one sentence.
questions.answer:
The wave is transverse. The pattern travels horizontally, while the medium displacement is vertical, so
\[
\vec \xi\perp \vec v_w
\]

questions.prompt: A compression wave in a spring has speed \(6.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and period \(0.20\,\mathrm{s}\). Find the spacing between successive compressions.
questions.answer:
The spacing between successive compressions is one wavelength:
\[
\lambda=v_wT=(6.0)(0.20)=1.2\,\mathrm{m}
\]

questions.prompt: A student says, "If a marked particle in the medium is moving left at one instant, the wave must also be moving left." Explain why this conclusion is not valid.
questions.answer: The motion of one particle in the medium is not the same thing as the motion of the wave pattern. A particle can momentarily move left while the crest or compression pattern moves right. To determine propagation direction, track a fixed phase point such as a crest or compression as time passes.

questions.prompt: Two waves travel along the \(+x\)-direction with the same \(\lambda\) and \(f\). In wave A the medium displacement is always along \(\hat y\). In wave B it is always along \(\hat x\). Compare their classifications and explain why equal \(\lambda\) and \(f\) do not force the same wave type.
questions.answer:
Wave A is transverse because its displacement is perpendicular to propagation:
\[
\vec \xi_A\perp \hat x
\]
Wave B is longitudinal because its displacement is parallel to propagation:
\[
\vec \xi_B\parallel \hat x
\]
Equal wavelength and frequency only imply equal phase speed
\[
v_w=f\lambda
\]
They do not determine the direction in which the medium oscillates, so they do not determine the wave type.

questions.prompt:
A wave propagates along \(+x\) and the local displacement is
\[
\vec \xi(x,t)=a\hat x\cos(kx-\omega t)+b\hat y\cos(kx-\omega t).
\]
Give the conditions on \(a\) and \(b\) for the wave to be purely longitudinal, purely transverse, or neither.
questions.answer:
The propagation direction is \(+x\), so compare the displacement vector with \(\hat x\).

- Purely longitudinal: the displacement must be entirely along \(\hat x\), so \(b=0\) and \(a\neq 0\).
- Purely transverse: the displacement must be perpendicular to \(\hat x\), so \(a=0\) and \(b\neq 0\).
- Neither purely longitudinal nor purely transverse: both components are present, so \(a\neq 0\) and \(b\neq 0\).

If \(a=b=0\), there is no wave disturbance at all.
